title: Non-blocking findings from frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups's re-review of PR #416 (post path-traversal-fix round)
description: pr-reviewer's re-review of PR #416 (after task-worker's commit 413f22df closed the path-traversal bypass with a normalizing custom ESLint rule) accepted the PR -- the rule was proven genuinely active via a mutation test, the traversal bypass was independently reproduced as fixed for static/dynamic imports and newly-tested re-export forms, type-only handling was confirmed correct in every shape tested, and the full coverage/static-analysis/e2e suites all passed with no regression. Two non-blocking findings surfaced during this review round that weren't caught by either the prior rounds or the backgrounded code-review pass, and shouldn't disappear once PR #416 merges.

checklist.step: The blocked-path regex `BLOCKED_SRC_VALUE_IMPORT = /(^|\/)src\/(?!utils(?:\/|$))/` anchors on `(^|/)`, which matches not just a project-relative `src/` segment but also a bare npm package specifier that happens to contain a literal `src/` path segment anywhere in it -- e.g. `import { x } from 'my-package/src/foo'` is incorrectly flagged as blocked, verified empirically (`path.posix.normalize('my-package/src/foo')` is unchanged, and the regex matches the `/src/` substring right after `my-package`). This is a real false positive not present in the original six-directory glob-allowlist version of this rule (which only matched specific `**/src/<dir>/**` globs, never a bare `src/` segment inside an unrelated package name) -- introduced when PR #416 replaced the allowlist with the default-deny regex, and unchanged by this round's traversal-bypass fix since the regex's anchor shape didn't change. No e2e spec in the current tree imports a package whose specifier contains a literal `src/` segment, so nothing is misflagged today, but it's the same class of over-restriction as the already-fixed bare-utils-barrel false positive, just on a different input shape. Worth either tightening the regex to only match a `src/` segment that's actually relative-path-rooted (e.g. requiring the source to start with `.` or `/`), or at minimum documenting this as a known limitation in Testing.md alongside the other disclosed gaps.

Board-bookkeeping pattern worth deciding explicitly: task-worker folded the already-filed follow-up task (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups) into PR #416/the parent task's branch -- marking its checklist items done, setting its `git.branch` to the parent task's own branch name rather than a dedicated `task/<its-own-id>` branch, and resolving both tasks' states together. This was an explicit, documented judgment call (a `decisions` entry gives the rationale: avoiding a redundant branch/PR pair for a three-line fix in the same file) and didn't trip any `validate_tasks.py`-checked structural invariant, but CLAUDE.md's board conventions don't explicitly address a 'fold a follow-up task into its parent's same-round fix' pattern, and the child task's `git.branch` diverged from the `task/<task-id>` naming convention CLAUDE.md documents. Worth either formalizing this pattern in CLAUDE.md's board-conventions section (when it's acceptable for one PR/branch to resolve two task ids, and how `git`/`state` should be recorded on the piggybacking task) or deciding it should always get its own branch/PR regardless of diff size.

decisions.decision: Fixed checklist item 1's bare-package-specifier false positive by requiring the *raw* (pre-normalize) import source to start with `.` before `isBlockedSrcSource` even calls `path.posix.normalize()`/tests `BLOCKED_SRC_VALUE_IMPORT` against it, rather than checking the normalized source's leading character or trying to make the regex itself package-aware.
decisions.rationale: A bare npm package specifier (`my-package/src/foo`, `@scope/pkg/src/foo`) never starts with `.` per Node/bundler module resolution semantics, so gating on the raw source's leading character rules those out before the `src/`-segment test ever runs, with zero risk of reintroducing either previously-fixed hole: a `..`-traversal specifier (`'../../src/utils/../api/homework'`) still starts with `.`, so it still reaches the normalize-then-test step unaffected, and the bare-`src/utils` barrel exemption is untouched since it lives entirely in the regex's lookahead, not in this new gate. Checking the raw source rather than the *normalized* one was a deliberate choice, not an equivalent alternative: `path.posix.normalize('./src/foo')` strips the leading `./` down to `'src/foo'`, so gating on normalized-starts-with-'.' would have let a single-dot-relative specifier silently slip through as if it were a bare package specifier -- gating on the raw string avoids that edge case entirely, even though no current e2e spec happens to use a single-dot relative import. Considered and rejected: (1) making the regex itself require a path-separator-anchored `src/` some other way (e.g. `(^\.|/)src\/`) -- functionally similar but less obviously correct/auditable than a short-circuiting early-return gate with its own explanatory comment; (2) resolving each specifier against Node's actual module-resolution algorithm (e.g. via `require.resolve`/an import map) to definitively distinguish package vs. relative -- massive overkill for a lint rule whose only job is catching the common case, and ESLint's own rule execution model (no filesystem resolution, no bundler context) doesn't cheaply support it anyway. Verified with manual probe imports placed in `tests/e2e/__probe.ts` (removed before commit, confirmed via `git status`) covering every case in the task's checklist item 1, plus a mutation test (temporarily inverting the new gate's boolean) that flipped ESLint's output as expected, proving the rule construct is genuinely active rather than silently inert.

decisions.decision: Left checklist item 2 (whether CLAUDE.md should formalize or rule out the 'fold a follow-up task into its parent's same-round fix, same branch/PR' pattern used for PR #416) unresolved and `done: false`, and did not edit CLAUDE.md or anything under `.claude/` in this PR.
decisions.rationale: This is a product/process-governance call about the task board's own conventions, not an ordinary implementation judgment call this worker has standing to make unilaterally -- and per CLAUDE.md's own 'Autonomous pipeline' rule, a PR touching CLAUDE.md or `.claude/` cannot be merged by `pr-merger` and requires an explicit human merge, so bundling a CLAUDE.md edit into this otherwise fully-mechanical, easily-mergeable fix would have blocked it on that unrelated governance question. The two live options for whoever does pick this item up: (a) formalize the pattern in CLAUDE.md's board-conventions section -- define when it's acceptable for one PR/branch to resolve two task ids (e.g. a follow-up small enough to land in the same diff as its parent's fix), and how `git.branch`/`git.pr_number`/`state` should be recorded on the piggybacking task (point `git.branch` at the parent's branch with a note, or require it to still reference the parent PR's number even though it has no PR of its own); or (b) rule it out -- require every task, however small, to get its own `task/<id>` branch and PR, accepting the overhead of a near-trivial PR for a three-line fix in order to keep the one-task-one-branch invariant exceptionless and `git.branch` always literally matching `task/<task-id>`. Recording this as a `decisions` entry rather than a `questions` entry because the task instructions for this PR explicitly pre-decided the disposition (checklist item 2 stays `done: false`, no `.claude`/CLAUDE.md edit) -- there's nothing left here that only the user can answer *for this PR*; the open governance question itself is already fully described in the checklist item's own text, so restating it as a separate `questions` entry would be redundant. This leaves the task not fully complete by design -- the reviewer should expect checklist item 2 to remain open and not treat it as an oversight.

comments.summary: Re-proved the e2e-import-guard/no-restricted-src-import rule is genuinely active (full 12-shape probe matrix reproduced, plus a mutation test inverting the new startsWith('.') gate that flipped the flagged/allowed set exactly as expected). Re-reproduced the two previously-fixed holes (path-traversal bypass still flagged static+dynamic; bare src/utils barrel still allowed) to confirm the new gate didn't reintroduce either.

Scrutinized the raw-vs-normalized split for a reachable gap: no tsconfig paths/baseUrl, vite resolve.alias, or package.json subpath imports exist in this project, so a no-leading-dot specifier (e.g. 'src/features/x', '/src/...') has no resolver path to the project's own src/ tree and isn't used anywhere in the current tree -- not a reachable gap given this repo's actual tooling.

Confirmed docs/architecture/Testing.md's updated prose accurately describes the raw-vs-normalized split and relative-specifier gate, and confirmed the PR's diff genuinely does not touch CLAUDE.md or anything under .claude/, consistent with checklist item 2 being left done:false by design.

Full suite re-run clean: backend ruff/mypy, frontend eslint/tsc, profit-target wording guard, pytest (1655 passed, 99.95% coverage), vitest (1083 passed, ~99.8% coverage), make e2e (28/28), validate_tasks.py (no violations). No regressions, no new findings.

Correction to this review's own comment above about the raw-vs-normalized scrutiny: a backgrounded code-review pass (launched during this same review, returned after the verdict below was posted) found that the new `isBlockedSrcSource` gate also un-flags a root-absolute specifier (`/src/pages/Something`), which main's pre-PR version of the rule did flag -- verified independently by checking out main's eslint.config.js and confirming it flags `/src/utils/format` while the PR's version doesn't, and by confirming via a throwaway `server.pluginContainer.resolveId()` probe that Vite's own dev-server resolver *does* resolve a root-absolute specifier like `/src/utils/format` against the project root (so this isn't a purely theoretical specifier shape for this toolchain). So the earlier comment's "not a reachable gap" framing was incomplete for the leading-slash case specifically (it only fully holds for the no-leading-dot, no-leading-slash case, e.g. `src/features/x`). However, this is judged non-blocking, not a reason to reopen: (1) `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` independently rejects the same specifier with `TS2307: Cannot find module`, and `static-verify`'s tsc step is already a mandatory part of this project's own review gate, run clean on every PR including this one; (2) empirically running an e2e spec containing this import through the actual `yarn playwright test` runner fails hard with `Error: Cannot find module '/src/pages/Something' imported from ...` before any test executes, because Playwright's Node-based test runner resolves a leading-`/` specifier as an absolute filesystem path, not as Vite-root-relative -- so there is no working, silent bypass of the e2e black-box boundary this rule exists to protect, only a narrower error-reporting mechanism (tsc/runtime crash instead of eslint) for an already-unreachable-in-practice specifier shape. Tracked as a non-blocking finding on frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups (tighten the gate to also reject a leading `/`/`~`, or disclose it in Testing.md as a known residual gap the way the dynamic-template-literal case already is).

The same backgrounded code-review flagged that the custom e2e-import-guard/no-restricted-src-import rule has no persisted automated test of its own -- every fix across this rule's history (allowlist->regex, path-traversal bypass, bare-utils-barrel false positive, this PR's bare-package-specifier false positive) is verified only via a manual probe file written, run through `yarn eslint`, and deleted before commit. Confirmed this pattern in this review too (my own verification used the same throwaway-probe approach). Non-blocking, but a real recurring gap -- each round has found a different edge case in the same regex-based logic that a persisted test matrix would have a better chance of catching going forward. Tracked on the same follow-up task.

review.notes: Independently re-verified task-worker's bare-package-specifier fix for PR #416's false positive. Re-proved rule liveness via mutation test, re-reproduced both previously-fixed holes (traversal bypass, bare-utils barrel) to confirm no regression, and scrutinized the raw-vs-normalized split for a reachable gap. Testing.md's updated prose matches the implementation. Checklist item 2 correctly remains open by design (governance call deferred to a human, since a CLAUDE.md/.claude/ edit can't be merged by pr-merger) -- this PR's diff does not touch either path. A backgrounded code-review pass launched during this review returned its result only after the verdict below was first posted; its two findings (a root-absolute-specifier gap in the new gate, and the rule's lack of a persisted automated test) were independently re-verified and are recorded above, plus tracked as a follow-up task (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups) per CLAUDE.md's non-blocking-finding tracking rule. Verdict remains accepted: both findings are real but non-blocking -- the root-absolute case is independently caught by this project's own mandatory tsc gate and fails hard at actual Playwright test-run time (no silent, working bypass), and the missing-test gap is a pre-existing pattern across this rule's whole history, not something this specific PR introduced or made worse.

pr_decision.notes: Re-ran both suites clean (pytest: 1655 passed, 99.95% coverage; vitest: 1083 passed/104 files, ~99.8% lines) and both static-analysis pairs (ruff, mypy, eslint, tsc -b --noEmit all clean), matching pr-reviewer's reported numbers. Skimmed the full diff (frontend/eslint.config.js, docs/architecture/Testing.md, docs/tasks/index.json, the two task JSONs) myself. Independently reproduced the backgrounded-review's root-absolute-specifier finding from scratch rather than trusting its text: confirmed via a throwaway node script that main's isBlockedSrcSource flags '/src/pages/Something' while PR #417's version returns false for it (though its own cited example '/src/utils/format' is exempted on both main and the PR since src/utils/ is always allowed -- a minor inaccuracy in the review comment's specific example, not in its substantive claim); confirmed via `server.pluginContainer.resolveId('/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx')` that Vite's dev-server resolver does resolve a root-absolute specifier against the project root; then independently confirmed the two claimed backstops myself rather than taking them on trust -- a probe e2e spec importing '/src/utils/format' is NOT flagged by `yarn eslint` under this PR's rule, but IS rejected by `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` (TS2307: Cannot find module) and crashes `yarn playwright test --list` outright ('Error: Cannot find module ... imported from'). So this is a real, newly-introduced lint-level false negative, but not a 'nothing catches it' silent gap: it's redundantly caught by tsc (a mandatory part of this project's own static-verify gate) and by the actual e2e runtime's own module resolution, both of which fail before any test could run or merge silently -- unlike the my-package/src/foo false positive deferred on PR #416, this doesn't meet the 'defeats the guard's purpose with nothing to catch it' bar for hard-blocking, since something robust does catch it. Concur with pr-reviewer's non-blocking classification and with the follow-up task (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups) already filed for it. On the missing-persisted-test structural finding (its checklist item 2): a real and legitimate process gap given four consecutive rounds of edge cases in the same regex-based logic, but it's pre-existing across this rule's whole history and not something this specific, narrow PR introduced or worsened -- my view is it's worth prioritizing as a precondition for the *next* change to this rule's logic, not a retroactive blocker on this already-correct, already-reviewed fix. Accept holds.
